recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. Revisit only if a future publisher/build regression omits inherited constraints or other aggregable ElementDefinition content from generated snapshots, or drops ElementDefinition.constraint.source provenance needed to distinguish inherited constraints during rendering.
issue_request: FHIR-12179 was Published/Persuasive for DSTU2 and asked the official build snapshot to inherit all applicable constraints from applied base and type profiles, with ele-1 applied to all elements as the example. Jira comments also clarified that mappings, aliases, and other aggregable ElementDefinition content were included in the intended snapshot inheritance.
initial_application: Jira records svn revision 10025 as the application. In Git history this is commit 82e1ca4af69d33f527a180c7bfa003e811feb4c0, whose subject names Tasks 12180, 12182, and 12179. The visible source change added ElementDefinition.constraint.source so inherited constraints can be retained in snapshots while preserving their originating StructureDefinition for rendering and traceability.
additional_context: Current build scope includes ElementDefinition as an active datatype and StructureDefinition as an active resource. Current StructureDefinition source says specialization snapshots include inherited elements and rules; profiling guidance says generated snapshots are complete and inherited constraints are retained; StructureDefinition notes explain inherited constraints are propagated into snapshots with ElementDefinition.constraint.source. A current CI build check of Patient.name in patient.profile.json shows ele-1 inherited from http://hl7.org/fhir/StructureDefinition/Element, with inherited mappings also present.
reconciliation: Published an empty audit commit. The historical build/source change was applied, current authoritative source documents the retained-in-snapshot behavior, and current generated output demonstrates inherited Element constraints such as ele-1 are present in snapshots with source provenance.
